title: Flatness of the tensor square and weak etaleness descend along a faithfully flat extension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes ring maps A -> B -> C and asserts two descents: that if B -> C is faithfully flat and C tensor_A C -> C is flat, then B tensor_A B -> B is flat; and that if B -> C is faithfully flat and A -> C is weakly etale, then A -> B is weakly etale (source lines 30374-30383). The proof of the first part is a descent along the displayed commutative square with corners C tensor_A C, C, B tensor_A B and B. The proof notes that the vertical arrows are flat and the top horizontal arrow is flat, whence C is flat as a B tensor_A B-module (proof lines 30385-30395). The substantive step is the descent: since B -> C is faithfully flat and C = B tensor_B C, the flatness of C over B tensor_A B descends to flatness of B over B tensor_A B, by the general descent lemma for flatness (proof lines 30395-30398). The second part then follows from the first together with the fact that A -> B is flat whenever A -> C is flat and B -> C is faithfully flat, again by the same descent lemma (proof lines 30399-30401). The non-routine content is the arrangement of the base-changed square so that the flatness of the top arrow plus faithful flatness of B -> C gives the conclusion by descent.
